title: TNM classification of lung cancer, 9th edition (IASLC, UICC, AJCC version 9)
sections: The 9th edition of the TNM classification for lung cancer keeps the T descriptors of the 8th edition unchanged. It subdivides N2 into N2a, metastasis in a single ipsilateral mediastinal or subcarinal lymph node station, and N2b, metastases in multiple ipsilateral mediastinal or subcarinal stations, counted regardless of N1 involvement. It subdivides M1c into M1c1, multiple extrathoracic metastases in a single organ system, and M1c2, multiple extrathoracic metastases in several organ systems.

In the 9th edition T1 N1 M0 moves from stage IIB to stage IIA, T1 N2a M0 becomes stage IIB, T2 N2b M0 becomes stage IIIB and T3 N2a M0 becomes stage IIIA. T2 N2a M0 and T1 N2b M0 are stage IIIA, T3 N2b and T4 N2a or N2b are stage IIIB, N3 disease is stage IIIB with T1 or T2 and stage IIIC with T3 or T4. M1a and M1b remain stage IVA and both M1c1 and M1c2 remain stage IVB.

In a validation cohort of 4029 people with resected NSCLC, restaging from the 8th to the 9th edition moved 151 patients from stage IIB to IIA and 57 from IIIB to IIIA, and the 9th edition gave clearer overall survival separation between stages IIA and IIB.
verified: Checked against Rami-Porta et al., J Thorac Oncol 2024 (PMID 38447919) as reported in Annals of Surgical Oncology 2025; validation figures from BMC Cancer 2024 (PMC11603870).

title: TNM classification of lung cancer, 8th edition (IASLC, UICC 2017)
sections: In the 8th edition, N2 was a single category for ipsilateral mediastinal or subcarinal nodes: T1 N2 and T2 N2 were stage IIIA and T3 N2 and T4 N2 were stage IIIB, T1 N1 and T2 N1 were stage IIB, and M1c was a single category staged as IVB. The 8th edition has been replaced by the 9th edition.
verified: 8th edition stage table as published by the IASLC staging project (Chest 2017).
